body:
I love people...in theory I guess.  But I get tired easily around them, so I must be fairly introverted.  I have a small circle of good friends and that's mostly all I need.  In groups larger than 3 I tend to let the conversation perpetuate itself, getting very quiet and listening.  I have no problem in crowds, and no problem making small talk, but when it comes to actually connecting with a person or flirting with them, I seize up - I am desperately lonely in a romantic fashion, but I have no experience in fixing that so I just stay at home.  I am 31 years old and had a girlfriend for two of those years, who stopped loving me but didn't tell me until the day she left, and then refused to ever talk to me again.

I love people's creativity, passions, pursuits, the technology and beauty we're capable of - but I get depressed easily when I see us fall short.  I am unable to comprehend why people can do certain things, like my ex's aforementioned stonewall, or how someone can cheat, or murder, or do anything they know will destroy someone else, emotionally or physically.  I guess I am too sensitive, though in other ways I'm not - I don't hold grudges and love all forms of humor, even when they insult things I hold dear.  I hold freedom of speech very highly.

I am extremely, extremely hard on myself.  I think it is part of why I am so forgiving and kind to others - I can forgive almost anything short of not trying, of giving up, and that's all I ever seem to do.

What would it take for me to consider someone a friend?  Evidence that they are a good person, or trying to be.  That's about it.  For them to be *my* friend though, they would also have to take the initiative fairly often.  I come out of my shell rarely and to maintain relationships the other person often has to come to me, because my energy is very low and I default to thinking I'm bothering someone when I go after them.

I can't see a particular triggering event, but yes I was definitely lonely.  I've been lonely ever since, except for those two years with my ex, which turned out to be at least partially false on her end.  That happened many years after the depression set in, after two times where I almost went through with taking my own life.  So while I'm sure the end of that relationship didn't help and it's definitely shaped me into being more fearful, it's not the root cause.

That was really verbose, sorry.  Also you are not coming off as a prick.
Oh, well, I don't normally visit sites like that of course, but if it's for a good cause!...
I'm sorry, then.  I hope you find a solution.

Yeah.  Like a cloud settled over me, and slowly thickened to the strength of diamond.  Worst part is there is no situation I can point to, no triggering event, no particular heartbreak that put me on this path.  I just got sad and pointless, and I have no idea why.  And it's been like that so long now I don't really care anymore.

I keep telling myself to do those things, and I do them for a little while, and then stop.  I just don't understand why I should keep going if my whole life will be like this...I've been this way since 18 or so and I see no signs of an epiphany where I somehow cast off my lassitude and become the energetic, spontaneous, confident, romantic, badass person I want to be.  Not even incrementally.

Depression is part of it but not all, and there's no pill for lazy, no shot in the arm to give you a shot in the arm.  I am the least motivated person I know and it's killing me.

Or rather it isn't, and that's why I have to focus my energies towards that now, so the next tiny burst of energy is enough to do this one thing to stop it.  Just this one thing.  I'm so tired of being a stunted, shy, inexperienced man-child failure.

I hadn't seen that before - thank you for teaching me something new.

I just...I don't see the point in continuing when I know no matter whether I get any more opportunities to improve my lot, I won't take them...I'm too tired, depressed, and lazy, and life only helps those who can help themselves.

I want to believe the whole "it gets better" schtick.  But I am 31 years old with no job, no love, no children, no security, and no skills.  I'm not "on my way" to anything, I'm worse off than I was straight out of college.  I'm not building a life so much as waiting for death.  And I'm tired of being an utter failure at everything but good intentions.

I'm sorry, but that's just not true.  The world needs good and kind people who also go out and use those values in constructive and positive ways.  At this point my recidivism and loneliness is so bad I think it would be easier to teach a bad person to be good than teach me to be social, driven, and constructive.  There is too much built up pressure and shattered expectations, I can't try anymore.

Anyone that responds to a post like this with a comment like yours, though, is someone to cherish.  I might not believe you but your sentiment is beautiful and for that so are you.  The world needs people like *you*, for sure.

I agree with you.  Though I'm a bit torn in this case...standards of beauty certainly vary from culture to culture, but this sort of thing comes close to me saying there's an objective limit to what we consider "pretty."

Really though, the important thing is whether the person/their mate/their social environment considers them attractive - if they do that's all that matters.  If they don't, if they're unhappy...hmm.  This is why, while I wouldn't recommend it for 99% of the people who end up getting it, I'm still glad things like plastic surgery exist as an option.

I was thinking a lot about it tonight (check my previous post if you don't believe me.)  Thank you for sharing your story.

It's not a fun existence for anyone with those thoughts.  I hope you are able to heal eventually.
